$comment: D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE (TF-C73): GNU `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` is HONORED — the alignment is APPLIED, not merely parsed — and applied IDENTICALLY in every position that can carry it: LEADING (`__attribute__((aligned(32))) int g;`), AFTER-DECLARATOR (`int h __attribute__((aligned(64))) = 7;`), COMPOSITE AFTER-KEYWORD (`struct __attribute__((aligned(32))) CK {…};`), MEMBER (`int v __attribute__((aligned(16)));` inside `struct M`), and COMPOSITE TRAILING (`struct CT {…} __attribute__((aligned(32)));`). Each position is gated by a RUNTIME ADDRESS CHECK and/or a `sizeof`, never by a diagnostic count or by merely compiling: the failure mode of an alignment sink is a wrong applied value that emits NOTHING, so only an observed layout can catch it. g -> exit 1, h -> 2, CK sizeof -> 3, &ck -> 4, M sizeof -> 5, &m.v -> 6, CT sizeof -> 7, &ct -> 8; all correct -> h + 35 = 42. ★★ EVERY CHECK IS PROVEN NON-VACUOUS, per check, by isolating it into its own program and building it three ways (sink ON / `aligned` effect demoted `align`->`none` / `declarationAttrSlotRules` removed from the structSpec row). The full matrix is in main.c's header. This matters because it CORRECTS A MEASURED DEFECT in the previous revision of this example: it had NO offset breakers, so the first over-aligned global in each section landed at a page-aligned section start and `&g % 32` / `&h % 64` / `&k % 8` held whether or not the sink ran — three of its five checks COULD NOT FAIL, including the AFTER-DECLARATOR position this example exists to prove. The whole-file 42->1 it reported as its red came entirely from the leading check firing once other globals shifted around it, an accident of ordering rather than a property of the check. `bss_pad` / `data_pad` (one byte, same section class, immediately before each over-aligned object) make the natural placement differ from the aligned placement; DO NOT delete them, and do not add an over-aligned global without one. ★ THE TYPEDEF ROW WAS REMOVED, not fixed: `aligned(8)` on `unsigned long long` asks for exactly the alias's natural alignment, so no padding arrangement can make it discriminate — it is vacuous by construction. Its real, observable behavior is COMPILE-TIME (over-alignment refused loud, S002F; MEASURED) and is pinned there. An honest absence beats a check that cannot fail. ★ THIS EXAMPLE DISCHARGES A PINNED PROMISE: `examples/c/gnu_attribute_after_declarator/` had to drop `int v __attribute__((aligned(4))) = 20;` when the trailing position started being scanned (accepting it there meant SILENTLY DROPPING the alignment), recording that the case returns 'when the real `aligned` sink lands, asserting the ALIGNMENT, not merely the parse'. It returns HERE, address-checked. ★ The two COMPOSITE rows close what the previous revision recorded as 'NOT COVERED, because the surface does not exist yet' (it was S0031, fail-loud); the after-keyword slot landed one cycle after its grammar was first written and reverted, because the composite attribute scan then read a single surface and would have dropped a leading `packed` in silence. RED-ON-DISABLE (OBSERVED, via patched config trees under `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT`, live checkout untouched): demoting the `aligned` effects row to `"none"` moves rows 1/2/5/6 to a wrong NUMBER and rows 3/4/7/8 to a COMPILE error (the composite scan refuses an attribute it cannot honor rather than dropping it) — so under that switch the composite rows abort the compile and the runtime checks never run, which is precisely why the proof isolates each check instead of reading one whole-file exit code. Removing `declarationAttrSlotRules` from the structSpec row moves ONLY rows 3/4, isolating the composite lead surface this cycle added. The `release` arm is MANDATORY, not decoration: the point is witnessing that the real SHIPPED optimizer PRESERVES the alignment rather than re-laying-out the globals. The whole file is VERIFIED clang-clean (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang-built binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain — a corpus example must witness REAL C, not merely C that DSS happens to accept.
